text:
pagerbot: ALERT: autoscale:us-east-1 - sustained throttle events detected (tokens/sec spike) across inference-pool-3. Autoscaler attempted 3 scale-ups in 5m, 2 failed. Current queue_depth=420, tokens/sec=18500, throttle_count=47. Dashboard: https://grafana.internal/r/redwood/autoscale?panel=throttle

maria: oncall here, seeing the same. paging eng-runtime and eng-sre. I'm going to lock new requests to the canary route to reduce fanout :slightly_frowning_face:

jonathan: looking now — logs show repeated OOM attempts when starting new worker pods, kernel messages about device memory pressure. suspect driver/kernel mismatch on recent node image in the fleet.

alex: @maria good call on canary lock. I'm spinning up manual capacity in the dedicated pool as a temporary bypass (cmd: `rctl capacity allocate --pool inference-pool-3 --gpu 8 --reason "incident 1799002460"`). Will post when done.

maria: thanks @alex. maria -> jonathan: can you confirm whether the node image rolled out in the last 6h?

jonathan: yes, node-image v2.14 rolled at 02:03 UTC. I see ~60% of the new nodes reporting nvml errors. Opening a quick kernel/driver scrub across the group.

nina: customer-impact note: some customers on dedicated tiers reported increased tail latencies and 502s. No full outages yet. Recording customer messages in #support-escalations.

sam: running a targeted query against time-series to characterize the alerts:
```
promql: sum(rate(throttle_events_total{pool="inference-pool-3"}[1m])) by (instance)
```
results: spike aligns with a burst of long context requests (avg seq_len ~12k tokens) from a single tenant.

maria: mitigation plan so far: 1) manual capacity bump by @alex 2) lock canary route to stop traffic split 3) short-term rollback of node-image to v2.13 on affected cluster (if confirmed) 4) throttle back very long-context requests via per-tenant guardrail.

ops-liaison: FYI I've informed sales/CS and created incident ticket: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-7543 — added customer-impact tag and expected update cadence every 30m.

jonathan: quick update — we confirmed driver mismatch. Rolling nodes back to v2.13 on the affected ASG. Initiating cordon/drain on bad nodes. Expected stabilization in ~12m.

maria: take 20 to stabilize then we do a status & handoff. If CPU/memory pressure subsides, we can release the canary lock and let autoscaler resume.

(12m later)

pagerbot: INFO: node health restored for inference-pool-3; 6/6 nodes passed NVML check. Autoscaler resumed.

maria: verified throttles decreasing. current tokens/sec=5200, throttle_count=2, queue_depth=95. Nice work.

nina: customers reporting latency improvements. I'll keep watching support threads.

sam: postmortem note candidate: root cause = node-image v2.14 introduced NVML driver mismatch causing worker initialization failures, which blocked autoscaler from successfully provisioning fresh capacity; result: short-term capacity starvation and throttle spikes when long-context requests hit.

alex: ops/action: revert the rollout pipeline gating to include quick NVML smoke before full ASG rollout. Also creating a short-lived policy to allow manual capacity overrides to bypass standard init checks for emergency (requires 2 approvals).

maria: now discussion about alerts & dashboards. Current problem we hit: 1) throttles triggered repeatedly and paged oncall even though autoscaler was already trying to scale 2) alert noise from brief spikes from single tenant long-requests 3) no dedicated dashboard panel showing pending worker init failures which would have pointed to driver errors faster.

jonathan: proposed immediate alert changes (temp):
- Reduce sensitivity of throttle rate alert: change evaluation window from 1m to 5m (to avoid short burst pages)
- Add an alert that fires when autoscaler reprovision attempts > 2 in 10m AND init_failures > 1 (this should surface init errors instead of throttles)
- Add suppression when manual scaling is in-progress (detect via capacity allocation events)

sam: +1. Also suggest adding a percentile-based token/sec metric: alert if tokens/sec p95 > X for 5m AND queue_depth p95 > Y for 5m to avoid being driven by single-instance noise.

nina: for customer-facing slackops runbook: recommend proactively messaging tenants doing very long-context requests to use batch APIs or gating (we already have guardrails but we should be explicit in runbook).

maria: action items created: INC-2026-7543-POST (post-incident tuning and runbook) and ENG-OPS-2026-511 (dashboard + alert changes). I'll own the runbook update. @jonathan please own the alert changes and add the init_failure panel. @alex please add the quick-smoke gate to the rollout pipeline.

alex: acknowledged. I'll also add a temporary Grafana panel to show 'pending worker init failures' by node and attach it to the incident dashboard.

jonathan: will implement alert rule changes in alert-manager now (testing in staging first). snippets: 
```
- alert: AutoscalerInitFailureSpike
  expr: increase(init_failures_total{pool="inference-pool-3"}[10m]) > 1
  for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: critical
```
(then tie to paging only if autoscaler reprovision attempts > 2)

maria: one more post-incident decision: queue_depth-based paging threshold seemed too low for heavy-context workloads. Propose raising queue_depth page threshold from 300 -> 600 for pooled inference routes but keep per-tenant throttling at current levels. We can compensate by making the throttle_rate alert more sensitive to tokens/sec p95. Thoughts?

sam: agree with raising queue-depth threshold for pooled pools. We should, however, add a new alert scoped to single-tenant long-requests: fire when tenant_request_token_count p95 > 8k for 10m -> pager. That isolates noisy tenants.

nina: capture customer comms: we should ask customer teams to opt into bulk-processing path or use a dedicated pool for long-context jobs. I'll draft the comms.

maria: ok — timeline: jonathan to push alert changes to staging in next 1h, alex to add rollout smoke in PR today, runbook and dashboard updates by EOD. We'll re-evaluate in the postmortem meeting tomorrow 14:00 UTC.

ops-liaison: noted — I'll add the actions & ETA to the incident ticket and set followups. Closing this page for now; reopen if any regressions. :white_check_mark:
